The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Appellant/accused Nos.1 to 3 feeling aggrieved by order of the trial Court on the file of II Additional District and Sessions Judge Uttara kannada, Karwar in Mundgod P.S. crime No.61/2023 dated 08.06.2023, preferred this appeal.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge Uttara kannada, Karwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Parties to the appeal are referred with their ranks as assigned in the trial Court for the sake of convenience.

3. The factual matrix leading to the case of prosecution can be stated in nutshell to the effect that in the month of June, 2022, victim-complainant came into contact with accused No.1 and accused No.1 knowing full well that victim-complainant belongs to schedule caste was in love with her and both of them were working in Bangalore.
They had come to Ranebennur for Ganesh festival.
Accused No.1 kept NC: 2023:KHC-D:7550 victim-complainant in the house of his friend Yasmin K.T, where she was residing along with her mother.
Accused No.1 on the promise of marrying victim disproportionately touched her private parts without her consent and committed sexual intercourse.
Thereafter, both of them came back to Bangalore.
On completion of training joined jobs by residing separately in P.G.
Accused No.1 under the promise of marrying victim was moving with victim-complainant in Bangalore.

Thereafter, accused No.1 left Bangalore stating that he will go to Prasad Kumar S/O Prakash Bhadangakara vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41579534/
2 his native place i.e. Mainalli village by saying that he will come back to Bangalore after one week.

entities.text: Prakash Bhadangakara vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, accused No.1 did not come back to the Bangalore.
On 15.05.2023 victim-complainant went to Mainalli village to the house of accused No.1 and informed to parents of accused No.1 about herself and accused No.1 being in love with each other.
However, all accused started abusing victim in filthy language by taking her caste.
The parents of accused No.1 did not approve the marriage of accused No.1 with victim-complainant.
The C.D.P.O, Mundgod arranged the victim to stay in Sadana Santwana Kendra.
On the same day, in spite of advice, accused No.1 refused to marry her at the instigation of accused Nos.2 and 3.

On these allegations made NC: 2023:KHC-D:7550 in the complaint, case is registered in Mundgod P.S. Crime No.61/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 354(A) and 376 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(w), 3(2)(5a) of the Schedule Caste and Schedule Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 (hereinafter referred to as "Act").
4.

entities.text: Schedule Caste and Schedule Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The investigation officer during course of investigation arrested accused Nos.1 to 3 on 19.05.2023,
since then they are in judicial custody.
The appellants/accused approached the trial Court for seeking regular bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
The trial Court after hearing of both sides by order dated 08.06.2023, rejected the bail application.

5. Learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 has filed objections contending that there are sufficient material evidence against all the accused for the offences alleged against them,
the consent of victim is becomes immaterial.

There are sufficient prima facie evidence to show that accused No.1 has committed sexual assault on victim, further all the accused have abused victim-complainant in filthy language by taking her caste with an intention to humiliate the NC:
2023:KHC-D:7550 complainant in public view.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of appeal.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 filed memo adopting the same objections filed by respondent No.1.

7. Heard the arguments of both sides.
8.

On careful perusal of the complaint allegations, it would go to show that, accused No.1 committing sexual assault on victim-complainant took place on 29.08.2022 in the house of one Yasmin K.T, who is friend of accused No.1 was residing along with her mother.
Thereafter, both victim and accused No.1 moved to Bangalore and thereafter, on undergoing training joined different jobs by staying in PG.

The complainant came to Mainalli village on 15.05.2023, since accused No.1 did not come back to Bangalore as assured and victim-complainant informed the parents of accused No.1 about victim and accused No.1 being in love with each other.
However, all the accused have abused the complainant in filthy language by taking caste of complainant with an intention to humiliate in public view.
The complaint came to be filed on 18.05.2023.
The trial Court has rejected the bail application of all the accused on the ground that the offences alleged against accused are non-bailable and they are serious in nature.

Further, accused have abused complainant in filthy language by taking her caste with an intention to humiliate in public Prasad Kumar S/O Prakash Bhadangakara vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41579534/
3 view.
10.

entities.text: Prasad Kumar S/O Prakash Bhadangakara vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for appellant has contended that even if the allegations in the complaint are accepted that sexual assault was committed on victim against her consent then said act of accused No.1 has been condoned, since admittedly they lived together in Bangalore for considerable period of time.

Whether accused Nos.2 and 3 intentionally insulted or intimated with intent to humiliate complainant being member of schedule caste or schedule Tribes within public view in terms of Section 3(1)(r) of Schedule Caste and Schedule Tribes attracting the penal in terms of Section 3(2)(5a) is a matter of trial.

11. Indisputably, even according to the victim as per the complaint allegations, accused No.1 is alleged to have committed sexual intercourse in the house of his friend one Yasmin K.T. in Mainalli village.
However, records produced by NC: 2023:KHC-D:7550 learned High Court Government Pleader, it would go to show that no any final opinion is recorded about sexual assault as alleged in the complaint.
The FSL report is awaited, further investigation is not yet completed and charge sheet has not been filed.
Insofar as the bail application of accused No.1 is concerned, there are material evidence to hold that accused No.1 has committed sexual assault on victim-complainant.

Under these circumstances, at this stage accused No.1 is not entitled for bail and he can move fresh bail after charge sheet is being filed.
12.

Insofar as accused Nos.2 and 3 are concerned, who are the parents of accused No.1, the allegations against them as per FIR is that they abused victim-complainant in filthy language and refused to perform the marriage accused No.1 with victim.
The said incident even according to victim took place in front of the house of accused.
The user of abusive words by taking caste of complainant is arising out of victim informing the parents about their love affair and they refused to perform the marriage of accused No.1 with victim.
Whether such abusive words was intend to humiliate the victim in public view is a matter of trial.

Insofar as offence under Section NC:
2023:KHC-D:7550 3(2)(5a) of the Act is concerned, the same is related to imposition of sentence, if the schedule offence is proved.

13. It is not the case of victim that the parents accused No.1 were also knowing that the victim belongs to Schedule Caste and they were aware about love affair of accused No.1 with victim-complainant, so that inference can be drawn of their knowledge to humiliate the victim in public view.
Hence, under these circumstances, in my opinion, there was no justification for trial court to refuse the bail application of accused Nos.2 and 3.
The apprehension of learned HCGP can met by imposing appropriate conditions.

Consequently, proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Appeal filed by the appellants is hereby partly allowed.

The order of the trial Court on the file of II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Uttara Kannada,
Karwar, in Mundgod P.S. crime No.61/2023, dated 08.06.2023 is hereby set-aside insofar as appellant/accused Nos.2 and 3 are concerned.

ii) Appellant/accused Nos.2 and 3 shall furnish address proof document of himself and that of their surety.
iii) Appellant/accused Nos.2 and 3 shall not leave the jurisdiction of trial Court without it's prior permission.
iv) Appellant/accused Nos.2 and 3 shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses in any manner or to contact the victim-complainant.
